messages:
alicia: Hey team — alerting because private-vpc pool us-west1-prod-runtime started showing a sustained p95 spike around 23:40 UTC. p50 ~65ms, p95 ~420ms, and overall RPS fell ~30%. Noticed during a canary load run. 

mike: :eyes: I see correlated increase in egress queue length on the NAT nodes in that VPC. `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` shows backlog growth. Could be conntrack saturation or MTU propagation issues.

dina: FYI I rolled kernel-selector change 2h ago that forces kernel-optimized sendpath for Llama-like arches on that pool. Rollout id: ks-roll-2026-03-18-21. Could be a regression in the kernel path selection. deploy-bot: ks-roll-2026-03-18-21 applied to us-west1-prod-runtime (5 nodes) :white_check_mark:

samir: KV cache hit-rate hasn't changed dramatically (p95 kv lookup latency flat), but the number of concurrent inflight requests per instance spiked. `curl -s http://runtime-metrics/summary | jq .inflight` showed jump from ~12->~42. Might be batching heuristics misfiring and holding requests in the runtime.

leo: I pulled a perf profile from one of the affected pods. Top stacks show a lot of time in `__x64_sys_sendto` and context-switch helpers. Also see increased `skb` clones in netdev. Paste: ```
# perf top snapshot
40.2% __x64_sys_sendto
11.3% __schedule
8.9% tcp_tso_finalize
6.4% net_tx_action
```

mike: That aligns with egress bottleneck — large batches hitting kernel TSO path and causing CPU/queuing. If kernel-selector picked a path that favors bigger send batches, it could aggravate NAT bandwidth and MSS issues.

alicia: Can we confirm if MTU/MSS clamping changed? infra-bot: NAT gateway config update applied 2026-03-18T21:05Z by infra-ops — changed `mss_clamp` from off -> on on 3 gateways.

dina: Hmm I didn't touch NAT. That was infra-ops change to mitigate some fragmentation alerts earlier. If mss_clamp is on, it should reduce fragmentation, but a mismatch between batching output and MSS can still cause stalls.

samir: Quick checks I ran: `conntrack -S` shows conntrack entries near the max (85% of nf_conntrack_max). `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` current=235000. Also `ss -tun sport = :443` shows many TIME_WAIT/TCP_CLOSE_WAIT states.

leo: Also found a cluster-level iptables rule that was re-added by an automation job around the same time — a LOG rule on egress that runs on a subset of customers. `iptables -w -L NAT-LOG -n -v` shows packet counts rising. Logging can drastically increase CPU overhead on NAT nodes.

mike: So likely multi-factor: kernel selector rollout changed send path -> larger kernel-side batching/TSO -> NAT egress with logging + conntrack near saturation -> increased queueing -> runtime batch heuristics backpressure -> higher latencies and lower throughput. Noisy neighbor effect from logging rule/conntrack memory.

alicia: Actionable next steps? I'm leaning rollback kernel-selector rollout for the pool and disable the iptables LOG rule on the NATs, plus bump conntrack as hotfix.

dina: I can do rollback of ks-roll-2026-03-18-21 in the canary pool now (2 nodes) and watch. If that improves, we revert for rest.

mike: I can coordinate with infra to remove the LOG rule and temporarily set `nf_conntrack_max` + apply `conntrack -F` on the worst nodes after cordon/drain. But need infra approval for conntrack flush.

infra-bot: infra-ops requested for change: remove NAT LOG rule from us-west1 gateways, requested by mike. Pending approval.

alicia: OK let's do rollback first to avoid touching infra state. DINA, roll back and paste the rollout revert id. We'll monitor p95 and queue stats. If no improvement in 6m, proceed with LOG rule removal + conntrack bump.

dina: Rolling back now -> revert-ks-2026-03-18-21 applied to 2 canary nodes :hourglass_flowing_sand: will post when p95 stabilizes.

leo: For postmortem, we should add a perf regression check in kernel-selector CI that simulates NAT egress (TSO path) and a guardrail to avoid enabling sendpath increases on private VPCs with constrained NATs. Also add a hook that alerts if iptables LOG rules exceed X packets/min.

samir: Agreed. Also add KV cache/backpressure metric export: number of requests queued by batching heuristic and average hold-time. That would have caught the heuristic holding too long when egress stalls.

alicia: Thanks all. Please update this thread with revert id and key metrics. Ping @mike when you remove LOG rule. :thumbsup:
